# Understanding updates

## Moving date

*Historical state after the posts were read. This uncertainty was subsequently resolved by Rowan’s correction below.*

**Updated 2026-11-06 after reading the selected posts.** The initial story followed Rowan’s interview and read: “The move was from the parents’ flat to a room above a bakery in Bellwick, in late August 2019, Rowan thinks.” The [original answer](../80_Sources/Interviews/2019-first-move.md#answer-1) remains unchanged.

The new [post published 2019-09-09](../80_Sources/imports/c8b6e8bbe42ebbc4a58c8f213d0ffa6f89e5ae5bb9a9efbcb0ba20c0ddfc3508-r1.md#^record-c8b6e8bbe42ebbc4a58c8f213d0ffa6f89e5ae5bb9a9efbcb0ba20c0ddfc3508-r1) says “Two days after moving” and “Kit carried the books up two flights on Saturday.” Those relative dates point to 7 September 2019 if the publication date and wording are literal. The record also labels the event “The Saturday before this post.” This conflicts with the approximate late-August memory; the supplied sources do not resolve why. Neither the older post nor the newer recollection has been declared automatically correct.

The story now leaves the date unresolved and cites both accounts. The timeline represents one move with conflicting dates. A future clarification could establish whether either date refers to a different stage of moving, but no such explanation is assumed.

## What the posts add

The September table was borrowed from Kit’s aunt, not a gift. Its expected winter return in [the September post](../80_Sources/imports/7a8a469d4d19a731e24b37949ac5c8e813d46189c925f3544672361e599e6cbb-r1.md#^record-7a8a469d4d19a731e24b37949ac5c8e813d46189c925f3544672361e599e6cbb-r1) is distinct from Rowan’s [January report](../80_Sources/imports/98764f41a20d7976640e3045e0d89f8691c7f47223239df66d7cc769c9c32754-r1.md#^record-98764f41a20d7976640e3045e0d89f8691c7f47223239df66d7cc769c9c32754-r1) of having returned it in December. The desk is known to be present by the January post; no acquisition date was supplied.

The saucepan was not found on moving day according to the first post. This can coexist with Rowan’s recollection of calling Mum to ask where it was; the account does not invent a successful find that evening.

## Date correction

**2026-11-06, subsequent owner clarification.** [Rowan’s correction, 2026-11-06](../80_Sources/Interviews/2019-dates-correction.md#correction) explicitly says the August date was a mistake and quotes a calendar entry: “7 September 2019 — moved into the room over the bakery, Kit brought the books.” The calendar itself was not inspected. This is specific corrective testimony consistent with the September post, rather than a choice to trust whichever source is newest. The story, profile and timeline now use 7 September 2019. The original interview, imported post and prior reconciliation text remain intact.

The same clarification expands the January post’s “in December” into Rowan’s handover to Kit on 19 December 2019, followed by Kit’s return to their aunt. The earlier narrative said: “By the post of 12 January 2020, Rowan had returned the table to Kit for their aunt ‘in December.’” This was an edited summary, reproduced here with typographic quotation marks adjusted. The precise handover now appears in the actual story, Kit’s page and chronology. Kit’s onward handover date is still unknown; it is not assumed to be the same day.

The train trip provides Rowan’s stated reason for remembering 19 December. No route, destination or trip narrative is inferred. The desk’s acquisition date remains unknown. No source text was rewritten to conceal the earlier uncertainty.
